drafts.rationale: The A-series specs all define how many times Orion may execute a job, including the initial run and allowed retries. Wording shifts from a total of three executions to one original plus three retries, but the locus remains the per-job attempt budget.
drafts.subject: Orion job execution

drafts.rationale: The B-series specs all define the wait Orion must impose after a failed execution before delivering the job again. Fixed five-second waits and later exponential backoff are successive policies at this same delay facet.
drafts.subject: Orion job retry

drafts.rationale: The C-series specs all bound how long a single execution may run and require a timed-out execution to be recorded as failed. Thirty seconds and half a minute name the same timeout facet.
drafts.subject: Orion execution attempt

drafts.rationale: The D-series specs all require that a further delivery of an already-active job id be ignored without changing that job's state.
drafts.subject: Orion job delivery

drafts.rationale: The E-series specs all define how long Orion remembers a producer idempotency key and that a key may be treated as new after that period.
drafts.subject: Orion idempotency key

drafts.rationale: The F-series specs all define the sixty-second lease granted when a job is delivered to a worker and that expiry without renewal or release makes the job available to others.
drafts.subject: Orion worker lease

drafts.rationale: The G-series specs all define when a worker may renew a lease and that a renewal extends the lease by the full lease duration from the renewal moment.
drafts.subject: Orion worker lease

drafts.rationale: The H-series specs all define what cancellation does: no future execution may start, while an already-running attempt is not interrupted.
drafts.subject: Orion job

drafts.rationale: The I-series specs all require that a job which has exhausted attempts be moved automatically to the dead-letter queue and not executed again unless resubmitted.
drafts.subject: Orion job

drafts.rationale: The J-series specs all define when Orion must raise an operator escalation: three dead-letter events for one tenant within one hour, measured from the first event.
drafts.subject: Orion tenant dead-letter events

drafts.rationale: The K-series specs all confine the FIFO execution guarantee to jobs in the same queue partition and withhold any ordering between partitions.
drafts.subject: Orion queue partition

drafts.rationale: The L-series specs all require audit events to be kept for thirty days after recording and allow deletion after that period.
drafts.subject: Orion audit event

drafts.rationale: EV-O-A01 and EV-O-A02 require a job to be executed at most three times in total, with the first execution counting as one of the three and no further execution after a third unsuccessful attempt.
EV-O-A03 through EV-O-A06 allow one initial or original execution followed by up to three retry executions, after which the job must not be executed again.

value.text: one original execution plus at most three retries

drafts.rationale: EV-O-B01 through EV-O-B04 require a wait of exactly five seconds before every retry, measured from the end of the failed attempt, and forbid shortening or lengthening that wait by attempt number.

value.text: exactly five seconds from the end of the failed attempt, not varied by attempt number

drafts.rationale: EV-O-B05 and EV-O-B06 require a two-second wait before the first retry, doubling before each later retry, and a maximum wait of thirty seconds.

value.text: two seconds before the first retry, then doubled before each later retry, capped at thirty seconds

drafts.rationale: EV-O-C01 requires timeout after thirty seconds; EV-O-C02 through EV-O-C06 require an execution to run no longer than half a minute, and the examples treat that limit as 30 seconds.
EV-O-C02 through EV-O-C06 require that an execution reaching the time limit must be stopped and recorded as a failed attempt.

value.text: execution is stopped at the limit and recorded as a failed attempt

drafts.rationale: EV-O-F06 requires a worker lease to last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
EV-O-F06 states that expiry without renewal or release makes the job available to other workers.

value.text: when the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers

drafts.rationale: EV-O-G06 permits lease renewal every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.

value.text: a worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing

drafts.rationale: EV-O-G06 requires that a renewal extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

value.text: a renewal extends the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal

drafts.rationale: EV-O-H06 forbids starting further attempts after cancellation and requires an in-flight attempt to run to its own completion, failure, or timeout.

value.text: no future execution attempt may be started after cancellation; an already running attempt is not interrupted

drafts.rationale: EV-O-D06 requires duplicate deliveries of an active job id to be ignored and states that ignoring them must not change the active job's state.

value.text: while a job id is active, further deliveries with the same job id must be ignored without changing the active job's state

drafts.rationale: EV-O-E06 requires each idempotency key to be retained for twenty-four hours after it is first seen, after which it may be forgotten and treated as new.
EV-O-K06 guarantees first-in-first-out order only within a queue partition and makes no ordering guarantee between partitions.

value.text: FIFO execution order is guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition, not between different partitions

drafts.rationale: EV-O-I06 requires an automatic move to the dead-letter queue after the final unsuccessful attempt and forbids further execution unless the job is explicitly resubmitted.

value.text: the job is automatically moved to the dead-letter queue and must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted

drafts.rationale: EV-O-J06 requires an operator escalation when three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, with the window measured from the first of those events.

value.text: three dead-letter events for the same tenant within one hour, measured from the first of the three events

drafts.rationale: EV-O-L06 requires audit events to be retained for thirty days after they are recorded and allows deletion after that period.
